metadata.note: Two connected lines serving southwestern-central New Hampshire, both branching off the Northern Railroad's Concord-West Lebanon corridor at Contoocook (see nh_concord_northern_railroads.geojson): the Concord and Claremont Railroad ran west from Contoocook through Hillsborough, Bradford, and Newport to Claremont, formed by an 1874 merger of the original Contoocook Valley Railroad (Contoocook-Hillsborough, opened December 1849) with the Sugar River Railroad (Newport-Claremont, incorporated early 1870s), under Northern Railroad control. The Peterborough and Hillsborough Railroad branched south from Hillsborough to Peterborough (built c. 1877-1878 per most sources, though one source cites 1871 -- flagged as a genuine date discrepancy in the available sourcing). Boston and Maine absorbed the Concord and Claremont in 1887 (as its 'Claremont Branch'); regular passenger service was discontinued in 1954, with a brief private revival (Claremont and Concord Railway) in 1954-55 and an even briefer 8-week tourist steam operation (Bradford-Sunapee, July 22 - August 25 1961) -- neither modeled as separate segments here. The Peterborough-Hillsborough line's Peterborough-Elmwood section was formally abandoned in 1942 after 1936 hurricane washouts. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap; the Bradford-Newport stretch (~22km) did not resolve to a plausible connected path and is a straight-line approximation between the real station towns.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contoocook_River_Railroad (Contoocook Valley Railroad chartered June 24 1848, opened Contoocook-Hillsboro December 1849, 14.7 miles; renamed Contoocook River Railroad October 1 1857; merged with Merrimac and Connecticut Rivers Railroad October 31 1873; Boston and Lowell leased 1884, Boston and Maine purchased 1890)

The Bradford-Newport stretch did not resolve to a plausible connected path (implausible-detour check triggered) and is a straight-line fallback.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era; the precise opening date of the Peterborough and Hillsborough Railroad (1871 vs 1877-1878, conflicting sources); precise passenger-service end date for the Peterborough-Hillsborough line specifically.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
